governed_construct: One consumption of shared (cross-component) state inside a React component or custom hook: (a) any read of a React context object — a call to a context-reading hook, a <Ctx.Consumer> render-prop element, or a class component's `static contextType` + `this.context`; or (b) a call to a global-store hook from a state-management library (react-redux useSelector/useStore/useDispatch, jotai useAtom/useAtomValue/useSetAtom, recoil useRecoilState/useRecoilValue, zustand store hooks).
interpretation: The rule prescribes React's Context hook as THE mechanism for state shared across components. An instance conforms only when it is a call to the `useContext` function exported by the 'react' module, however it is reached: named import (including under an alias such as `useContext as useStore`), `React.useContext`, or a namespace import (`R.useContext`); a same-file custom hook that wraps such a call is fine because the instance is the inner call. An instance violates when shared state is consumed any other way: a Context `.Consumer` render prop, `static contextType`, or a third-party store hook (Redux, jotai, recoil, zustand) — including when that store hook is imported under the local name `useContext`. Identity is decided by import binding, not by the callee's spelling, which is why the rule is T3. Files whose components only use local state (useState/useReducer not exposed through a provider) or props contain no instance and are NOT_APPLICABLE. Creating a context or rendering a `.Provider` is not itself an instance (it is the producer side). A file mixing a conforming useContext read with any non-conforming consumption is VIOLATED.
